newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor drops two pct on press interview.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor drops two pct on press interview.

text.p: Shares in Portuguese cement producer Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal dropped two percent on selling by domestic investors on the Lisbon bourse due to a press interview by the company's president, dealers said.

"The fall in Cimpor is due to the interview that the president of Cimpor Antonio Sousa Gomes gave to Publico newspaper in which he said the present share price is expensive," said one operator who asked not to be identified.
Cimpor stood at 3,312 escudos, down 68, in volume of 97,258 shares at 1034 GMT. Dealers said it could fall to 3,300 escudos soon.
Sousa Gomes told Publico that the Cimpor share price could fall eventually as small investors and employees who buy the shares at a discount later sell them at a profit.
Asked if the Cimpor share price was high, Sousa Gomes said: "Yes. And as small investors and employees, among others, have access to shares with a discount, this will certainly lead to a small drop."

The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres plans to sell off 45 percent of Cimpor in a second stage privatisation on October 15. The government will retain 35 percent. The government had previously sold off a 20 percent stake.
